Resolves #21652

On the home's plan preview the board's four columns now end on the Gantt chart's right edge, in every window from 1440 px up. The preview's stylesheet sets the board's width token to a clamp: the columns share the pane between 190 px and 212.25 px each, and 212.25 px is the width at which four columns span the chart (881 px). Below about 1260 px of window width nothing changes: the columns keep 190 px and the board scrolls.

Evidence: L2 (the preview rendered in the dev Portal: measured at six window sizes before and after, whole-page frames at three, the e2e spec with a mutation run, a real-mouse pass) → L2 required (AC-1 to AC-3). Residual: none.

Review focus: (1) the cap is a number of the snippet (881 px = 1 + 160 + 20 × 36), held in the stylesheet: a visitor who edits the snippet's time axis moves the chart's edge and not the board's. (2) AC-1 is read as the edge of the chart, not of the grid's box, which runs to the pane's edge at every width: [intake comment](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21652#issuecomment-7050201226).

Prescription checked: `resources/css/src/apps/portal/home/parts/Planning.css` owns the concern. It already sets the board's three tokens for this preview, and `src/board/Container.mjs:475-495` pins a column's `flex` and reads no width config, so the token is the board's sizing surface. No file under `apps/**` changes, so the app-work gate's reads were not run.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; the baseline jobs run in CI.

## Deltas from ticket

- **The board takes the chart's width, not the pane's.** The chart is 881 px wide in every window, and the pane is wider than that from about 1500 px of window width (1,209 px at 1920 × 1080). A board that fills the pane would run 320 px past the chart there. The ticket's comment holds the reading.
- **No blocker filed.** The board has no option for columns that share its width, and its token carries the preview's case, so the ticket's open question ends in one stylesheet line. Both engine gaps are recorded as defect-notes: `c9837d47` (a timeline cannot fit its viewport) and `146ca5f0` (board columns cannot share the width by a config).

## Test Evidence

**Measured on the rendered page** (dev Portal, Chromium, each size in a fresh context; x positions in px). "Chart" is the right edge of the time axis header, "last column" the right edge of the fourth board column.

| Window | Pane | Chart | Last column, released | Last column, now |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1280 × 800 | 476 → 1260 | cut by the pane | cut by the pane, the board scrolls 18 px | the same |
| 1440 × 900 | 529 → 1420 | 1411 | 1322 | **1411** |
| 1512 × 982 | 553 → 1492 | 1435 | 1346 | **1435** |
| 1920 × 1080 | 689 → 1900 | 1571 | 1482 | **1571** |
| 2560 × 1440 | 903 → 2540 | 1785 | 1696 | **1785** |
| 390 × 844 | 5 → 385 | scrolls | 800 px of columns in 378 px | the same |

**Mutation run.** With the stylesheet line reverted the new test fails at 1440 × 900: `Expected: <= 1, Received: 89`. With it, the spec's three tests pass locally (18.4 s).

**Real mouse** (1440 × 900, `mouse.down/move/up`): a click on "Data layer" selects it and highlights bar 5; "Prototype" dragged into Done lands there and its bar turns green; bar 5 dragged 52 px takes its three successors along; no console error or warning.

**Frames.** In each pair the released page is above and this branch below, 1:1.

![The plan preview at 1440 × 900: released above, this branch below](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/c368812b4f51bc5d1c659565ce5dd26f0cc32b78/review-evidence/21652/plan-1440x900.jpg?raw=true)

More: [1920 × 1080](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/c368812b4f51bc5d1c659565ce5dd26f0cc32b78/review-evidence/21652/plan-1920x1080.jpg?raw=true) · [390 × 844, released left and this branch right](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/c368812b4f51bc5d1c659565ce5dd26f0cc32b78/review-evidence/21652/plan-390x844.jpg?raw=true)

Frame critique: at 1920 × 1080 the board and the chart now end on one line at 73 % of the pane, and the pane's right quarter stays empty, as it did for the chart before: out of scope, noted in defect-note `c9837d47`. The board's first column starts 8 px right of the chart's left edge: that is the board's own padding on all four sides, kept.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

- **Challenge**:
  1. **On `Review focus (1)` + `TimeAxis.parseDayKey` local-midnight coupling (`src/timeline/TimeAxis.mjs:222-250`):** Holding `212.25px` (`(881 - 8 - 24) / 4`) in `Planning.css` is the right trade-off for the Engine 14 cut so `Planning.mjs` stays a clean 48-line domain snippet. Two coupled assumptions are worth keeping on the radar for when `defect-note` `c9837d47` and `146ca5f0` land: first, as noted in `Review focus (1)`, live-editing `timeAxis.end` or `pxPerMinute` in the Monaco `Source` tab moves `.neo-timeline-header`'s right edge while `.neo-board` stays capped at `881px`; second, `Planning.mjs` passes bare `'YYYY-MM-DD'` strings (`day(2)` to `day(22)`), which `TimeAxis.toDate` parses as viewer-local midnights (`parseDayKey`). For `2026-11-02..22` every IANA zone has zero DST transitions (`America/*` falls back on `2026-11-01` and `Europe/*` on `2026-10-25`, so `totalSize` is deterministically `28,800 × 0.025 = 720px`), whereas shifting the seeded window across a DST day would nudge the chart by `±1.5px`.
  2. **Phone evidence frame (`plan-390x844.jpg`):** Because `.neo-gantt` takes `height: 366` at the top of `.page-live-preview`, the un-scrolled `390 × 844` frame shows the Gantt half above the fold while `.neo-board` sits below it; verified directly from CSS arithmetic (`calc((362px - 24px) / 4) = 84.5px` → clamped to `190px`) and the body's `390 × 844` measurement row that the board's mobile column geometry is unchanged from `dev`.

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

*   **`[KB_GAP]`**: None.
*   **`[TOOLING_GAP]`**: None.
*   **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: In a flex `hbox` container with `box-sizing: border-box` and symmetric horizontal padding `P`, child percentage widths resolve against `W_border - 2P`, so `clamp(minCol, calc((100% - (N - 1) * gap) / N), (targetRight - P - (N - 1) * gap) / N)` aligns the last child's right border to an exact pixel target `targetRight` on wide viewports while smoothly sharing narrower panes down to `minCol` before scrolling.
